image_description: A close-up underwater photograph of a lionfish (Pterois) resting on a sandy, rocky seabed. The fish displays characteristic red and white vertical stripes, large fan-like pectoral fins with elongated rays, and prominent dorsal spines. The background consists of blurred coral or rock formations.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large head with prominent eyes and wide mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible in profile. The eye is distinct and prominent, and the mouth structure appears wide and consistent with scorpaenid anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed body with moderately sized proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is visibly laterally compressed (thin from top-down perspective, tall from side view), matching the biological description of a lionfish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brightly striped coloration in red, white, brown, or black bands.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows distinct alternating dark (reddish-brown) and light (white/cream) vertical bands across the body and fins.
While lionfish have small scales, the resolution of this image and the presence of skin texture/fins make individual scales indistinguishable to the naked eye. It is not testable at this zoom level.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal fin with numerous elongated venomous spines that fan outward like mane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal spines are clearly visible, elongated, and separated, fanning out from the back. They appear structurally independent and sharp.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large fan-like pectoral fins with elongated rays.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are large, semi-transparent, and show distinct, separate elongated rays spreading out like a fan.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pelvic fins also with elongated spines.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral/pelvic fins are visible beneath the body, showing the characteristic long, isolated spine/ray structure typical of lionfish.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification and rule out look-alike scorpaenids or generic fish hallucinations.
Lionfish fins are complex, thin structures prone to AI 'melting' or fusion with the background. This expert will verify the separation of individual rays and spines.
To assess general photorealism, lighting consistency, and detect subtle texture anomalies in the water/background interface.
To ensure the fish is properly grounded in the 3D space and not floating or bleeding into the rocky background.

focus_areas: Integrity of individual dorsal spines (no fusion/clumping)
Separation of pectoral fin rays (no webbing errors)
Boundary sharpness between fish fins and background rocks
Consistency of stripe patterns across body curvature
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the tips of the dorsal spines and the edges of the pectoral fins. AI models often struggle with these thin, high-frequency details, causing them to blur or merge with the background. Verify if the 'transparency' of the fins looks physically accurate or like a rendering artifact.
